In order to deflect the first magnet through $45^{\circ}$, the wire has to be twisted through $540^{\circ}$ whereas with the second magnet, the wire requires a twist of $360^{\circ}$ for the same deflection. Then the ratio of magnetic moments of the two magnets is
questions.solution:
If $C$ is torque per unit angular twist of the wire, then for a twist $\phi$,
$\tau=C \phi=M B \sin \theta$.
In the $1^{\text{st }}$ case, $\phi_1=540^{\circ}-45^{\circ}=495^{\circ}, \theta_1=45^{\circ}$
In the $2^{\text{nd }}$ case, $\phi_2=360^{\circ}-45^{\circ}=315^{\circ}, \theta_2=45^{\circ}$

Dividing (i) by (ii), we get
$\frac{M_1}{M_2}=\frac{495}{315}=\frac{11}{7}$

questions.q: An electron is travelling along the $x$-direction. It encounters a magnetic field in the $y$-direction. Its subsequent motion will be
options: a circle in the $x z$ plane
a circle in the $y z$ plane
a circle in the $x y$ plane.
questions.solution:
We know that the force on a charged particle $e$ due to a magnetic field is given by

$ \begin{array}{ll} 
& \vec{F}=e(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \\
\text{ Here } \vec{v}=v_x=\hat{i} \text{ and } \vec{B}=B_y \hat{j} \\
\therefore \quad & \vec{F}=e v_x B_y(\hat{i} \times \hat{j})=e v_x B_y \hat{k}
\end{array} $
Therefore the subsequent motion of the charged particle will be a circle in the $x z$ plane.
